content.text: In Zimbabwe, where PayPal and Stripe are restricted, digital creators face a critical infrastructure problem: how to sell [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-sell-ebooks-kenya-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/everything-you-need-know-about-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-plugins-without-payment-processor-which-architecture-actually-4|COREMERCH guide to selling]]-ebooks-nigeria|Everything You]]-you-need-get-2|ebooks]] and digital products without relying on platforms that charge exorbitant fees and limit access to their markets. With Gumroad charging 10% on every sale, and NOWPayments offering a 0.5% fee on crypto transactions, the difference in fees can retain $921 per month at 100 sales. To overcome this challenge, you need infrastructure that gives you full control over your payments and delivery pipeline. That's where COREMERCH comes in, providing a sovereign digital commerce stack that lets you sell ebooks and digital products on your own terms.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: How to Start Selling Digital Products with Crypto Payments at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/automated-digital-product-delivery-crypto-explained-digital-creators-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Bitcoin ebook

COREMERCH's sovereign digital commerce stack is designed to work around platform restrictions, giving you full control over your payments and delivery pipeline. With the Complete Builder Kit, you get access to all 6 blueprints and 7 templates, allowing you to build, deploy, and scale your own digital commerce stack. By using Cloudflare Pages and Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments, you can create a payment and delivery pipeline that is independent of platforms like PayPal and Stripe. This means you can sell ebooks and digital products on your own terms, without relying on third-party services that may charge high fees or limit access to your markets.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Pricing digital products in crypto is straightforward because NOWPayments handles the currency conversion automatically. You set your price in USD. The checkout pulls live exchange rates and displays the exact amount in whichever cryptocurrency the buyer selects. For USDT-denominated products, there is no conversion at all — one dollar in equals one dollar received, minus network fees that typically amount to less than $0.10 on Tron or Solana. You receive the crypto equivalent of your USD price in the wallet you configured in your NOWPayments account. COREMERCH never touches these funds at any point — the wallet is yours from the moment of setup and remains yours unconditionally.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase.
By using COREMERCH's sovereign digital commerce stack, you can reduce fees and increase scalability for your ebook and digital product sales.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

The order management layer gives you complete visibility into every transaction your store processes. In Stack 01, every order is logged to a Google Sheet with the buyer's email, product purchased, payment amount in crypto and USD equivalent, transaction hash for on-chain verification, and delivery status. In Stack 02, orders are stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with the same fields plus additional metadata. Both can be exported as CSV at any time. The transaction hash provides cryptographic proof of every payment that does not depend on any platform's records — you can verify any transaction independently on a public blockchain explorer.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Scaling a sovereign digital store requires no infrastructure changes at any realistic volume level for most individual creators. Cloudflare Workers processes each webhook event independently — ten simultaneous orders are handled as ten separate processes with no queue congestion. Supabase handles hundreds of concurrent database operations on the free tier. Resend delivers 3,000 emails per month on the free tier — enough for significant daily sales volume. Cloudflare Pages serves the storefront to any number of concurrent visitors without capacity constraints. NOWPayments processes payment volume without per-transaction approval delays.

By using Cloudflare Pages and Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments, you can create a payment and delivery pipeline that is independent of platforms like PayPal and Stripe.

If you're looking for more information on how to sell ebooks and digital products without relying on platforms that charge high fees, you may want to check out the Complete Builder Kit ($197) from COREMERCH. This comprehensive guide provides everything you need to build, deploy, and scale a sovereign digital commerce stack. Additionally, you can shop for other products on the COREMERCH website at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy COREMERCH's sovereign digital commerce stack, follow these concrete steps: set up a GitHub account and create a new repository for your project; obtain a NOWPayments account to accept crypto payments; configure NOWPayments to accept payments on your website; set up Cloudflare Workers to automate delivery of digital products; configure Supabase to store order data and track customer information; test your payment gateway and delivery automation; go live and process your first transaction.
